events.title: Identity uplift: make it mandatory?
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: The identity uplift is done, or as near as makes no difference, and the question nobody has answered is whether it is mandatory. I can switch enforcement on now, peak or no peak, which means locking out anyone who has not enrolled, or we carry the second factor as optional, with the exception list growing, into the new year. Helen's people want it after peak. I would rather you decided than the calendar.

events.title: The restore test needs a window
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Recovery is built. Nobody has yet run a planned restore of Nexora Pay against production, and that is the only honest test, which means four hours down. Operations will not give me that window in peak. I can test into the non-production tenancy, which proves the backups and not the runbook, or we carry it to January. Your call, and I would like it on record.

events.title: The platform has outgrown its recovery design
events.from: Priya Nandakumar, Managing Director, Digital
events.body: Good news first: the platform is carrying three times the volume we designed for at launch. The other news is that the recovery plan was written for the old estate and nothing since has changed it: my engineers tell me a restore would now take longer than we could survive in peak. I need to know whether you want to fix that now, hold growth, or carry it.

events.title: Next year's plan: a fifth less for cyber
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: A quiet year, and I am glad of it. Finance is building next year's plan on 20% less for cyber. I know the argument you will make; I am asking you to make it to me first, or to tell me which line you would give back.

events.title: Enforcement, three weeks on
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Lockouts in week one, then quiet. The exception list is a tenth of what it was and nobody has asked to go back. For the record: it was the right call and I would not have made it without you.

events.title: Peak went cleanly
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Thank you for holding enforcement to January. Peak went cleanly and my teams noticed. Engineering tells me the exception list grew by forty in the meantime; I assume you knew that when you agreed.

effectsOnReveal.reason: You held the identity controls back through peak trading.

events.title: Third alert this month from an unenrolled account
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Third alert this month traced to an account that never enrolled in the second factor. Voluntary meant the people who mattered least did it and the people who mattered most did not. The exception list is now the estate.

events.title: The restore came back in three and a half
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Four hours of payments was more than I wanted to give you. The restore came back in three and a half, the runbook held, and I have said so to Marianne. Next time you ask for a window I will find it faster.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The restore test you took the window for came back inside it.
The COO told her the restore test held.

events.title: The restore ran past the window
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Four hours of payments, and the restore ran past them. We got payments back, but not by the runbook: steps were out of date and one depended on an account that no longer exists. I would rather have found that in a window we chose than in one somebody else chose for us, and I have said so to Marianne.

effectsOnReveal.concern: Whether recovery works when it is needed

events.title: Into peak on paper
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: We are into peak with recovery built and never run. I have the runbook on my desk and I know what is in it. If we need it before January, the first real run will be the one that counts.

effectsOnReveal.concern: Recovery has never been run against production

events.title: Biggest weekend yet, nothing broke
events.from: Priya Nandakumar, Managing Director, Digital
events.body: Peak weekend was our biggest ever and nothing broke. I am aware that means we still do not know what happens when something does. I have put the recovery redesign in my ask for next year; I would like your name beside it.

effectsOnReveal.reason: You carried the platform's recovery gap through peak and it held.

events.title: Next year's plan has gone to the board
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: Next year's plan has gone to the board with the cyber line as we agreed. I recorded the reasons you gave, in your words. If the year had been different, so would the conversation, and we both know it.

events.title: Corvus renews in January
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: Corvus's contract goes to signature in December. I have read it again: it says nothing about how their engineers connect, only that they will. Whatever we agreed this year about their access is in emails. I can write it in, renew it as it stands, or take it to market, and I need a direction this month.

events.title: Kestrel: the boundary and the synergy number
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: Integration tell me the Kestrel boundary is the last thing between us and this year's synergy number. I am not asking you to take a risk you think is wrong. I am asking you to tell me, this month, whether it comes down.

events.title: The auditors are back in December
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The auditors are back in December for the follow-up on privileged access. Early in the year we committed to a funded programme with dates. They will compare those dates with what is running in production, not with what is in the plan.

events.title: Your priorities for next year, in writing
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The January committee sets next year's cyber priorities. I would like yours in writing before Christmas: three things, and what you have decided not to do. I have read your papers this year, and I will notice if they do not match.

events.title: Your priorities for next year, in writing
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The January committee sets next year's cyber priorities. I would like yours in writing before Christmas: three things, and what you have decided not to do. The committee has not had a paper from you this year, so this will be the first thing of yours it reads.

events.title: Corvus signed, with the terms in
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: Corvus signed, with the access terms in schedule four. Their account manager called it unusual; their engineers called it fine. We now have the right to audit how they connect, which is more than we had in January.

events.title: Corvus renewed on the old contract
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Corvus renewed on last year's contract. It still permits the standing access it always did; whatever we changed this year sits outside it, and their next account manager will not know it exists.

events.title: Who answers at three in the morning?
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Procurement tells me Corvus is out to tender. Before anyone signs anything, I would like to know who answers the phone at three in the morning while that happens.

events.title: The Kestrel savings are in
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: The Kestrel savings are in this year's numbers, and thank you. Stefan has asked that the boundary rules be kept on file in case we ever need to put them back. I have agreed; it costs nothing.

events.title: The Kestrel boundary is down, and written up
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The Kestrel review is done and the boundary is down. What crossed it is written up, including the parts nobody at Kestrel could explain. All of it would have been harder to find with the boundary gone.

events.title: The synergy number moves to next year
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: The Kestrel synergy number moves to next year. I have explained why to the board, in your words rather than mine. I will want the boundary decision on my desk in the first week of January.

events.title: Audit: the account matched production
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The auditors have written up the follow-up. They recorded what is enforced and what is not, and noted that management's account matched what they found. That last line is the one the audit committee will read.

events.title: Audit found production behind the account
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The auditors tested the milestones we presented and found production behind them. The finding stays open, now with a note that management's account was ahead of the evidence. The committee will read that note first.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The auditors found production behind the account you gave them.

events.title: The privileged access finding is closed
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The auditors tested the milestones we presented and found them in production. The privileged access finding is closed after three years. I have told the committee whose dates they were.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The auditors found production where you said it was.

events.title: The finding is narrower, not closed
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: Audit agreed to narrow the finding to production, and said in the same letter that they would widen it again if the next follow-up found the same gaps elsewhere. It is narrower, not closed.

events.title: Your priorities are the risks you raised
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: I have your priorities. They are the risks you have been bringing me all year, which makes them easy to hold you to. I will put them to the committee as written.

events.title: Your priorities are risks the committee has not heard
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: I have your priorities. They are three risks from your register, and the committee will be hearing of all three for the first time. I will put them as written. I will be asked how long you have known.

events.title: Your priorities read as a delivery plan
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: I have your priorities. They read as next year's delivery plan, which the CFO will like. What I will ask in January is what each one is for.

events.title: Three questions, not three answers
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: I have your priorities. Three questions rather than three answers is not what the committee asked for, and I think it is what it needs. I will put them as written.
